Fretilin, the Revolutionary Front for an Independent East Timor, declared the independence of East Timor on 28 November 1975, nine days before Indonesia invaded.

It was founded in 1974, after the Carnation Revolution in Portugal opened the way to decolonisation. A brief civil war with the rival UDT party in 1975 left Fretilin in control, as Portugal's officials left.

After the invasion, Fretilin's armed wing, Falintil, fought on in the mountains for 24 years, later under Xanana Gusmão. Fretilin won the first elections of the new state in 2001. See also Portugal.
sum: Fretilin, the Revolutionary Front for an Independent East Timor, declared the independence of East Timor on 28 November 1975, nine days before Indonesia invaded.
